arxiv-1403-1830.title: A short note on model selection by LASSO methods in a change-point model
arxiv-1403-1830.creator: Fuqi Chen, and, Sévérien Nkurunziza
arxiv-1403-1830.description: Abstract In Ciuperca (2012) (Ciuperca. Model selection by LASSO methods in a change-point model, Stat. Papers , 2012;(in press)), the author considered a linear regression model with multiple change-points occurring at unknown times. In particular, the author studied the asymptotic properties of the LASSO-type and of the adaptive LASSO estimators.

arxiv-2009-09215.title: Faster Smarter Proof by Induction in Isabelle/HOL
arxiv-2009-09215.creator: Yutaka Nagashima
arxiv-2009-09215.description: Abstract We present sem_ind , a recommendation tool for proof by induction in Isabelle/HOL. Given an inductive problem, sem_ind produces candidate arguments for proof by induction, and selects promising ones using heuristics. Our evaluation based on 1,095 inductive problems from 22 source files shows that sem_ind improves the accuracy of recommendation from 20.1% to 38.

arxiv-2104-08483.title: Proton correlations and apparent intermittency in the UrQMD model with hadronic potentials
arxiv-2104-08483.creator: Pengcheng Li, Yongjia Wang, Jan Steinheimer, Qingfeng Li, Hongfei Zhang
arxiv-2104-08483.description: Abstract It is shown that the inclusion of hadronic interactions, and in particular nuclear potentials, in simulations of heavy ion collisions at the SPS energy range can lead to obvious correlations of protons. These correlations contribute significantly to an intermittency analysis as performed at the NA61 experiment.

arxiv-2106-10134.title: An Audio-Driven System For Real-Time Music Visualisation
arxiv-2106-10134.creator: Max Graf, Harold Chijioke Opara, Mathieu Barthet
arxiv-2106-10134.description: Abstract Computer-generated visualisations can accompany recorded or live music to create novel audiovisual experiences for audiences. We present a system to streamline the creation of audio-driven visualisations based on audio feature extraction and mapping interfaces. Its architecture is based on three modular software components: backend (audio plugin), frontend (3D game-like environment), and middleware (visual mapping interface).

arxiv-2108-08380.title: Revisiting Binary Local Image Description for Resource Limited Devices
arxiv-2108-08380.creator: Iago Suárez, José M. Buenaposada, Luis Baumela
arxiv-2108-08380.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Iago Suárez, José M. Buenaposada, Luis Baumela. The advent of a panoply of resource limited devices opens up new challenges in the design of computer vision algorithms with a clear compromise between accuracy and computational requirements. In this paper we present new binary image descriptors that emerge from the application of triplet ranking loss, hard negative mining and anchor swapping to traditional features based on pixel differences and image gradients.

arxiv-2202-02112.title: Musical Audio Similarity with Self-supervised Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2202-02112.description: Abstract We have built a music similarity search engine that lets video producers search by listenable music excerpts, as a complement to traditional full-text search. Our system suggests similar sounding track segments in a large music catalog by training a self-supervised convolutional neural network with triplet loss terms and musical transformations.

arxiv-2305-12421.title: Evaluating Open-QA Evaluation
arxiv-2305-12421.creator: Cunxiang Wang, Sirui Cheng, Qipeng Guo, Yuanhao Yue, Bowen Ding, Zhikun Xu, Yidong Wang, Xiangkun Hu, Zheng Zhang, Yue Zhang
arxiv-2305-12421.description: Abstract This study focuses on the evaluation of the Open Question Answering (Open-QA) task, which can directly estimate the factuality of large language models (LLMs). Current automatic evaluation methods have shown limitations, indicating that human evaluation still remains the most reliable approach.

arxiv-2310-07058.title: Ion Trap with In-Vacuum High Numerical Aperture Imaging for a Dual-Species Modular Quantum Computer
arxiv-2310-07058.creator: Allison L. Carter, Jameson O’Reilly, George Toh, Sagnik Saha, Mikhail Shalaev, Isabella Goetting, Christopher Monroe
arxiv-2310-07058.description: Abstract Photonic interconnects between quantum systems will play a central role in both scalable quantum computing and quantum networking. Entanglement of remote qubits via photons has been demonstrated in many platforms; however, improving the rate of entanglement generation will be instrumental for integrating photonic links into modular quantum computers.

arxiv-2401-11166.title: ChatGPT in the classroom. Exploring its potential and limitations in a Functional Programming course.
arxiv-2401-11166.creator: M. Popovici a
arxiv-2401-11166.description: Abstract In November 2022, OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT – a chatbot based on supervised and reinforcement learning. Not only can it answer questions emulating human-like responses, but it can also generate code from scratch or complete coding templates provided by the user. ChatGPT can generate unique responses which render any traditional anti-plagiarism tool useless.

arxiv-2402-09757.title: Construction of CCC and ZCCS Through Additive Characters Over Galois Field
arxiv-2402-09757.creator: Gobinda Ghosh, Sachin Pathak
arxiv-2402-09757.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gobinda Ghosh, Sachin Pathak. With the rapid progression in wireless communication technologies, especially in multicarrier code-division multiple access (MC-CDMA), there is a need of advanced code construction methods. Traditional approaches, mainly based on generalized Boolean functions, have limitations in code length versatility. This paper introduces a novel approach to constructing complete complementary codes (CCC) and Z-complementary code sets (ZCCS), for reducing interference in MC-CDMA systems.

arxiv-2406-07665.title: Operators on complemented lattices
arxiv-2406-07665.creator: Ivan Chajda, Helmut Länger
arxiv-2406-07665.description: Abstract The present paper deals with complemented lattices where, however, a unary operation of complementation is not explicitly assumed. This means that an element can have several complements. The mapping + assigning to each element a a the set a + a^{+} of all its complements is investigated as an operator on the given lattice.

arxiv-2407-09424.title: TelecomGPT: A Framework to Build Telecom-Specfic Large Language Models
arxiv-2407-09424.creator: Hang Zou, Qiyang Zhao, Yu Tian, Lina Bariah, Faouzi Bader, Thierry Lestable, Merouane Debbah
arxiv-2407-09424.description: Abstract llm ( llm ) have the potential to revolutionize the 6g ( 6g ) communication networks. However, current mainstream llm generally lack the specialized knowledge in telecom domain. In this paper, for the first time, we propose a pipeline to adapt any general purpose llm to a telecom-specific llm .

arxiv-2504-08270.title: Kuga-Satake construction on families of K3 surfaces of Picard rank 14 14
arxiv-2504-08270.creator: Flora Poon
arxiv-2504-08270.description: Abstract The isometry between the type IV 6 and the type II 4 hermitian symmetric domains suggests a possible relation between suitable moduli spaces of K3 surfaces of Picard rank 14 14 and of polarised abelian 8 8 -folds with totally definite quaternion multiplication.

arxiv-2506-17841.title: Global Attractors of Non-autonomous Lattice Dynamical Systems
arxiv-2506-17841.creator: David Cheban, Andrei Sultan
arxiv-2506-17841.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by David Cheban, Andrei Sultan. The aim of this paper is studying the compact global attractors for non-autonomous lattice dynamical systems of the form u i ′ = ν ⁡ ( u i − 1 − 2 ​ u i + u i + 1 ) − λ ​ u i + f ⁡ ( u i ) + f i ​ ( t ) ​ ( i ∈ ℤ , λ > 0 ) u_{i}^{\prime}=\nu(u_{i-1}-2u_{i}+u_{i+1})-\lambda u_{i}+f(u_{i})+f_{i}(t)\ (i\in\mathbb{Z},\ \lambda>0) .

arxiv-2601-15757.title: White-Box m HC: Electromagnetic Spectrum–Aware and Interpretable Stream Interactions for Hyperspectral Image Classification
arxiv-2601-15757.creator: Yimin Zhu, Lincoln Linlin Xu, Zhengsen Xu, Zack Dewis, Mabel Heffring, Saeid Taleghanidoozdoozan, Motasem Alkayid, Quinn Ledingham, Megan Greenwood
arxiv-2601-15757.description: Abstract In hyperspectral image classification (HSIC), most deep learning models rely on opaque spectral–spatial feature mixing, limiting their interpretability and hindering understanding of internal decision mechanisms. We present physical spectrum-aware white-box m HC, named ES- m HC, a hyper-connection framework that explicitly models interactions among different electromagnetic spectrum groupings (residual stream in m HC) interactions using structured, directional matrices.

The most virulent strains belong to subspecies tularensis and these strains cause a sometimes fatal disease. Despite an intense recent research effort, there is very limited information available that explains the unique

pmc-11396935.title: Exploration of Compounds with 2-Phenylbenzo[d]oxazole Scaffold as Potential Skin-Lightening Agents through Inhibition of Melanin Biosynthesis and Tyrosinase Activity
pmc-11396935.creator: Hee Jin Jung, Hyeon Seo Park, Hye Soo Park, Hye Jin Kim, Dahye Yoon, Yujin Park, Pusoon Chun, Hae Young Chung, Hyung Ryong Moon
pmc-11396935.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Inspired by the potent tyrosinase inhibitory activity of phenolic compounds with a 2-phenylbenzo[d]thiazole scaffold, we explored phenolic compounds 1–15 with 2-phenylbenzo[d]oxazole, which is isosterically related to 2-phenylbenzo[d]thiazole, as novel tyrosinase inhibitors. Among these, compounds 3, 8, and 13, featuring a resorcinol structure, exhibited significantly stronger mushroom tyrosinase inhibition than kojic acid, with compound 3 showing a nanomolar IC50 value of 0.51 μM. These results suggest that resorcinol plays an important role in tyrosinase inhibition.

pmc-11417421.title: Blunt Trauma-Induced Lymphocele in the Groin — An Uncommon Complication and Management Considerations: A Case Report
pmc-11417421.creator: Thilina Gunawardena
pmc-11417421.description: Lymphoceles are common complications after certain surgical procedures. Blunt trauma can occasionally result in similar lymph accumulation. Herein, we present the rare case of a patient who developed a lymphocele in his right groin following a blunt trauma from a fallen tree branch. Aspiration and sclerotherapy were unsuccessful, and the lesion ultimately required surgical excision.

pmc-12441803.title: Case Report: Anthropometric profile and weight control strategies in a world boxing champion
pmc-12441803.creator: Rodrigo Yáñez-Sepúlveda, Carlos Abraham Herrera-Amante, Wiliam Carvajal-Veitía, Luis Aarón Quiroga-Morales, Diego A. Bonilla, Guillermo Cortés-Roco, Nicole Aguilera-Martínez, José Francisco López-Gil
pmc-12441803.description: PurposeThis case study aims to examine the anthropometric profile and body composition management of a Mexican featherweight world champion during key preparatory periods leading up to the World Boxing Organization (WBO) title fight. Special emphasis is placed on the strategic role of nutritional periodization in achieving optimal body composition while preserving performance capacity in a body mass-restricted, high-performance setting.

pmc-12598194.title: B‐Type Natriuretic Peptides Levels in Patients With Beta‐Thalassemia Major and Correlations With Biomarkers: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-12598194.creator: Mohamed S K Salih, Amna H Mohamed, Elsara M A Mirghani, Mohammed Y K Makki, Ola A M Ahmed, Esraa T S Mohammed, Hana HM Hassan, Nada Omar, Esraa M A Garalnabi, Sagad O O Mohamed
pmc-12598194.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPatients with beta‐thalassemia major are prone for developing cardiovascular complications. Early identification of patients at risk is important. B‐type natriuretic peptides such as brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N‐terminal pro‐BNP (NT‐proBNP) are sensitive indicators of cardiac dysfunction. This review synthesizes the existing evidence on the levels of B‐type natriuretic peptides in beta‐thalassemia major and their relationship with markers of cardiac dysfunction and other biomarkers.MethodsA systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines.

pmc-13031625.title: Comparative assessment of machine learning models for polymer solution viscosity prediction in enhanced oil recovery
pmc-13031625.creator: Sami Abderraouf Belkhir, Altamish Ahmed Pakeer, Mariam Shakeel, Rizwan Muneer, Younes Alblooshi, Muhammad Rehan Hashmet
pmc-13031625.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Polymer flooding is among the most researched and utilized methods to improve oil recovery. Polymer solution viscosity is the primary governing parameter that aids in lowering the mobility of the injected fluid and augmenting the volumetric sweep efficiency. However, the design of a polymer solution is time-consuming and requires intensive resources because of the need to design several precursors, including makeup water salinity, temperature, polymer concentration, etc., to sustain the target solution viscosity.

pmc-13195673.title: Hot-Carrier Injection and Millisecond Charge Separation from a Robust Heteroleptic Iron(II) Chromophore Immobilized on TiO2
pmc-13195673.creator: Thomas Whittemore, Marvin Schmalle, Evgenia Ryndin, Mark Spitler, Elias H. P. Brohmer, Sven Rau, Linda Zedler, Evgeny O. Danilov, Felix N. Castellano, Stephan Kupfer, Gerald Meyer, Dieter Sorsche
pmc-13195673.description: The synthesis, spectroscopic characterization, computational analysis, and photoelectrochemical behavior of a new iron-based chromophore, [(Cpy)2Fe­(deeb)]­(PF6)2 (Fe­(Cpy) 2 (deeb)), where Cpy is 1-methyl-3-(2-pyridyl)­imidazole and deeb is 4,4’-(CO2CH2CH3)2-2,2’-bipyridine, is reported. Electrochemically reversible waves assigned to a metal-centered Eo(FeIII/II) = +0.48 and a ligand-centered Eo(Fe2+/+) = −1.47 V vs Fc+/0 reduction were evident in cyclic voltammetry measurements.

pmc-13269341.title: Oncogenicity Variant Interpreter (OncoVI) Supports Harmonized Somatic Variant Interpretation in Precision Oncology
pmc-13269341.creator: Maria Giulia Carta, Lars Tögel, Annett Hölsken, Christoph Schubart, Heinrich Sticht, Robert Stöhr, Silvia Spoerl, Norbert Meidenbauer, Arndt Hartmann, Paolo Magni, Florian Haller, Fulvia Ferrazzi
pmc-13269341.description: Accurate and reproducible interpretation of somatic variants is fundamental for therapy decision-making in patients with cancer. To harmonize and automate oncogenicity classification, Oncogenicity Variant Interpreter (OncoVI), an open-source, Python-based implementation of the Clinical Genome Resource/Cancer Genomics Consortium/Variant Interpretation for Cancer Consortium oncogenicity guidelines, was developed.
